text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn accepted the resignation of two National Bank vice presidents Tuesday despite a call by central bank President Gyorgy Suranyi not to do so. @
- President Arpad Goncz on Tuesday appointed Judit Csiha as minister without portfolio in charge of privatisation and Szabolcs Fazekas as minister of industry, trade and tourism.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his Austrian counterpart Franz Vranitzky opened a 117 km natural gas pipeline Tuesday between Gyor and Baumgarten, thus decreasing Hungary's dependence on Russian energy sources.

- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti said Tuesday the government, if officially asked, is ready to recommend to Parliament that it assent to extending the mandate of the Hungarian IFOR contingent following its expiration. @
- Parliament's Constitutional Committee on Tuesday pinned responsibility for the recent privatisation scandal on a number of former top state officials in the privatisation arena.
- A Hungarian-Austrian-Slovak prime ministerial meeting will be staged in Postyen, Slovakia on November 4, said Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi.

- Klaus Haensch, chairman of the European Parliament, said in a speech before Hungary's Parliament that Hungary could be admitted to NATO in 1997, while negotiations on Hungary's full EU membership could begin in 1998. @

- The National Bank will make an advance debt payment of $1 billion, announced central bank president Gyorgy Suranyi, adding that the improvement in Hungary's rating shows the favourable prospects of the Hungarian economy.
- Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky laid the foundation stone of a huge department store on Tuesday in Szena ter which will be opened in 1998.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Hungarian and the Yugoslav defence ministers signed a military cooperation agreement in Budapest on Tuesday. @
- IMF representatives told Hungarian trade union executives Tuesday that Hungary has moved beyond the hard part of its economic transition.

- A senior Foreign Ministry official confirmed that the Swiss and the Hungarian governments concluded a pact in 1973 under which Switzerland paid 325,000 Swiss francs to Hungary from the accounts of Hungarian Jewish victims of the Holocaust.
VILAGGAZDASAG @

- An F-16 fighter made its debut at the Kecskemet air base Tuesday. Doug Miller, vice president of Lockheed Martin Tactical Aircraft Systems said his company would be delighted to take part in any cooperation project with Hungarian business partners.
- In order to decrease their outstanding debts, totalling HUF 250 billion, Hungary's health insurance and pension authorities will launch a debtor consolidation programme.
- The Belgian company Tractebel has acquired a majority stake in the Dunamenti Eromu power plant. @
- Price of Matav shares have increased by 50 per cent to 300 per cent of face value on the OTC market in the past two months.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The number of registered unemployed went up by 4,000 to 404,000 in the third quarter, according to the Central Statistics Office.
- The management of the pharmaceutical company Human will list the firm's shares owned by employees on the stock exchange.
